column1: # Directed, unweighted: edge A -> B when A's article wikitext links to B's,
# counting only inline links from the article's OWN prose/infobox -- links
# injected by shared navigation templates (e.g. the UN navbox) are excluded.
# Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda}. Kenya's intro sentence names all six as
# neighbors/border context in plain prose ("Kenya is bordered by South
# Sudan to the northwest, Ethiopia to the north, Somalia to the east...")
# without wikilinking any of them -- only "Lake Victoria" is bracketed in
# that sentence -- so the extraction rule correctly found zero out-edges
# for Kenya even though the source article clearly discusses all six.
# Added by hand rather than relaxing the extraction rule, which would
# require guessing at unlinked plain-text mentions article-wide.
# Belgium, Bosnia_and_Herzegovina, France, Germany, Italy, Japan,
# Montenegro, Netherlands, Portugal, Serbia, Spain, Switzerland,
# United_Kingdom, United_States}. Both articles had out-degree 0 for the
# same reason as Kenya: every country they mention -- bordering nations,
# colonial history, wars and treaties, trade partners, immigrant-origin
# countries -- is named in plain prose, never wikilinked. Found by
# scanning both articles' full wikitext (stripping <ref> citations,
# {{cite}}/{{sfnp}} templates, infobox flag-icon statistics tables, and
# image captions first, since a naive plain-text scan is mostly citation
# metadata and bibliography noise at this article length) for country
# names appearing outside [[double brackets]], then manually reviewing
# every hit for genuine substantive content. Included: bordering
# countries, named wars/treaties/historical rule, specific trade or
# investment fund centre, after the United States"). Excluded as
# incidental: open-ended comparison lists ("surpassed by the United
# States, Canada, Australia, ... and other small states like ...", which
# is what silently pulled in Australia/Canada/New_Zealand/Iceland/
# Monaco/San_Marino/Liechtenstein/Brunei on a first, less careful pass)
# and event-location mentions (Luxembourg exhibiting at an Expo "in
# Shanghai, China" is not a Luxembourg-China relationship; a photo
# caption naming "Helsinki, Finland" is not a Portugal-Finland one).
